text:
Sam (Customer): Hi support, after increasing traffic our /v1/rerank calls start returning intermittent 502/504s. p95 jumps from ~450ms to ~4s. Happening since 2026-06-03 09:12Z. Can you help?

Maria (Support): Sorry you're seeing that — can you share a sample payload + X-Request-ID from one failing call? Also your concurrency and candidate_count if known.

Sam (Customer): Sending sample: candidate_count=100, top_k=10, concurrency=120, RPS ~110. X-Request-Id: cust-22-req-20260603-091215. Payload snippet attached.

Dev Patel: thanks. Can you paste the exact error and response body when it 502s/504s? 504 from gateway usually means upstream didn't respond in time. 502 could be upstream crash or malformed response.

Sam (Customer): We get 504 with empty body sometimes, and once got 502 with: 
```
{"error":"upstream_error","message":"internal server error: runtime panic: oom"}
``` 
We also captured client-side timeout around 15s on some requests.

Nina (Runtime Oncall): Looking at infra metrics for that tenant: during the spike we saw pod mem usage climb and CPU saturate on the reranker pods. Kubernetes events show OOMKilled on two pods at 09:13:29Z. Autoscaler did spin up new pods but they were slow to become healthy.

Maria (Support): Any idea why candidate_count=100 would OOM? Our reranker models are pretty memory-hungry but we usually handle up to 64 comfortably, right?

Omar (ML): Correct. The reranker-v1 model maintains per-candidate key-value caches and performs cross-candidate attention in some layers; complexity can be O(n^2) relative to candidate_count in worst-case for intermediate memory. With candidate_count=100 and batch concurrency high, combined memory across requests can spike. Also note that some customers send long candidate strings which increase tokenization length and KV size.

Dev Patel: Repro plan: we'll run an internal k6 load with candidate_count=100, concurrency 120, RPS 100 to match their profile. Can you confirm endpoint and key to use?

Sam (Customer): Use their live key; they gave us a test key for support.

Nina (Runtime Oncall): Running repro now in a canary namespace to avoid customer impact. Early logs: when the reranker pod handles ~12 concurrent long-running requests, memory climbs past 80% and ephemeral swap triggers OOM. We also see our request router timing out after 10s and returning 504s.

Dev Patel: What are current timeouts in the gateway?

Nina (Runtime Oncall): Gateway timeout is 10s upstream, request-level default 30s. But the router upgrade path returns 504 when upstream exceeds gateway timeout. The reranker kernels sometimes hit long-tail due to large attention matrix compute (GPU kernels).

Maria (Support): Customer asked for immediate mitigations — what can we do server-side quickly?

Nina (Runtime Oncall): Short-term mitigations we can apply within 30m:
- set tenant config max_candidate_count=48 (server-enforced) -> requests >48 return 400 with helpful message
- enable per-tenant concurrency cap at 60 concurrent rerank requests -> extra requests get 429: Too Many Requests
- increase pod memory by switching to a larger instance type for this tenant pool (manual scale)

Omar (ML): Also can temporarily swap the tenant to a quantized reranker variant (reranker-q8) which uses ~30-40% less memory but slightly different scoring distribution. Need to warn customer about score drift.

Sam (Customer): We prefer a non-breaking change. Can you try the concurrency cap + informative 429s first? We can throttle on client side if needed.

Dev Patel: Agreed. We'll apply per-tenant concurrency cap, and add a response header X-RateLimit-Policy: tenant-concurrency=60 for visibility. Also will push a transient 429 body recommending candidate_count <= 48.

deploy-bot: rollout started: tenant-config-update(cust-22) -> apply to routing layer -> 2min canary -> full.

Nina (Runtime Oncall): Patch applied. We see immediate decline in OOMs for that tenant's reranker pods. p95 fell to ~700ms. A few 429s were returned as expected when client exceeded concurrent windows.

Sam (Customer): After applying a retry/backoff and lowering concurrency we observe much fewer 5xxs. Thanks.

Maria (Support): For transparency with the customer we should provide: 1) exact cURL to repro safe case 2) recommended client-side backoff strategy 3) timeline for ML fallback / long-term fix.

Dev Patel: cURL snippet to test safe config:
```
curl -sS -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Request-Id: support-test-01" \
  -d '{"query":"q","candidates":["short1","short2"],"candidate_count":48}'
```

Maria (Support): Backoff guidance: use exponential backoff on 429/503 with jitter. Suggested: initial delay 200ms, factor 2, max attempts 5, add full jitter. If 400 returned due to candidate_count, reduce candidate_count immediately.

Omar (ML): Long-term fixes we discussed: streaming candidate scoring (score in small groups to reduce peak memory), early-stopping heuristics when top_k stabilizes, lightweight embedding fallback, or a dedicated batching layer to cap memory per GPU. We should prioritize streaming scoring and embedding fallback.

Dev Patel: Filed support/engineering follow-ups:
- SUP-4329: customer mitigation applied and verified (support ticket)
- ENG-7110: implement tenant concurrency circuit breaker + better 429 payloads
- ENG-7111: reranker streaming scoring prototype (ML)
- ENG-7112: add alert: rerank.p95 > 2s sustained for 5m per-tenant

Nina (Runtime Oncall): Monitoring note: we added temporary dashboard cell for cust-22 showing pod OOM counts and p95. Will keep it for 48h. If no regressions, we can remove.

Sam (Customer): Confirming behavior improved. We'll keep candidate_count <= 48 in prod and will test embedding-fallback when available. Appreciate quick help.

Maria (Support): Marking ticket SUP-4329 as mitigated but not closed; will follow up when ENG PRs land. Adding all relevant logs and X-Request-Ids to the ticket.

Dev Patel: Final ops note: consider surfacing model score variance when swapping to quantized reranker (reranker-q8) so customers understand scoring drift. Also ensure we log model_variant and quantization flags in traces.

Nina (Runtime Oncall): Done. Thanks team. If anyone sees new 5xx spikes ping runtime oncall immediately. :pray:
